description: Orchestrator iteration 21 - draft one MECHANISM: line per handler for the 20 most-used arg_types whose generated ARG_TYPES.md entry is currently a use-case blurb, a mid-sentence fragment, or (float_scalar) a box-drawing separator. Strictly read-only; the orchestrator applies the lines. Split 10/10.

units.prompt:
READ-ONLY. Do not write any file. NO-GUESSING: every claim must come from code you actually read; if the code does not settle something, write [UNCERTAIN] rather than inventing. Never use 'probably'/'likely'/'appears to'.

BACKGROUND: `re/frida/ARG_TYPES.md` is GENERATED by scraping the up-to-3 `//` comment lines directly above each `if (CONFIG.arg_type === '<name>')` dispatch in `re/frida/diff_template.js`. That window often lands mid-sentence or on a decorative separator, and even when it reads cleanly it usually describes the handler's ORIGINAL USE CASE rather than its MECHANISM. A screen that asks 'does a handler exist for this shape?' then answers from those blurbs and wrongly concludes none fits. We are adding an explicit `// MECHANISM: ...` line that the generator will prefer.

YOUR JOB: for each of these 10 arg_types in `re/frida/diff_template.js`, read the handler's dispatch block (from its `if (CONFIG.arg_type === ...)` line down to the next dispatch) plus any comment block above it, and draft ONE `MECHANISM:` line.

  int_scalar (line ~398)
  void_write_observe (~4941)
  void_setter_observe (~537)
  scalars_to_scattered_globals (~4761)
  int_pair (~370)
  state_machine_observe (~741)
  struct_call_observe (~1213)
  ptr_arg_int_get (~413)
  entity_field_set (~621)
  ptr_seed_observe (~1314)

Each MECHANISM line must state, in this order and as compactly as possible:
1. The CALL SHAPE it can drive - argument kinds and how they are delivered (stack args, register args and WHICH register, out-pointers, buffers the harness allocates).
2. What it SEEDS before the call and what it OBSERVES after (return value? specific buffer offsets? absolute globals? recorded callee arguments?).
3. The CONFIG/registry fields that parameterise it (list the actual key names you see read from CONFIG or the hook entry, e.g. cfg.stride, CONFIG.observe, stub_at).
4. Any property that makes it apply MORE BROADLY than its name suggests - e.g. buffers shared across both sides so a stored pointer compares equal, or an offset that is configurable rather than fixed. THIS IS THE MOST VALUABLE PART: it is exactly what a screen needs and what the current text hides.

Hard rules:
- Describe the MECHANISM, not the function it was written for. Do not name specific game RVAs unless the handler hardcodes them.
- One line each, target 200-320 characters, no line breaks inside a line.
- If a handler genuinely IS narrow (only works for one hardcoded address or one fixed layout), say so explicitly - 'NARROW:' then why. A false claim of generality is worse than none.

OUTPUT FORMAT - exactly this, nothing else, one block per handler:

### <arg_type>
MECHANISM: <your line>
EVIDENCE: <file:line references you read, comma-separated>
